name: Solenoid Manipulation
description: Many electric locks use a solenoid to hold the bolt in the locked position. A strong neodymium magnet placed against the door surface near the solenoid can interact with the magnetic field of the mechanism, potentially releasing the lock. Effectiveness is highly dependent on door construction, solenoid type, and magnet strength and position. Works best on lighter electric strike assemblies where the solenoid is close to the door surface.

blue.det: Access control log shows door open without credential; video shows magnet application; fail-secure locks are completely immune.
blue.cm: Use fail-secure locks (locked when power is removed) instead of fail-safe on high-security doors; magnetic shielding in lock body; access control alerts on door open without credential.
